name: Mandelic acid peel

lead: A mandelic acid peel is a mild alpha-hydroxy acid peel used for acne-prone and sensitive or mature skin.
Only two small published studies were found: one on sebum in older women and one on adult acne in combination with salicylic acid.

paras: It is a superficial exfoliating peel; researchers have measured its effect on sebum secretion.
Authors of the sebum study describe it as mild with no side effects reported; light peels generally can cause stinging, redness and dryness.

lead: A mandelic acid peel uses mandelic acid, an alpha-hydroxy acid described as gentle in the aesthetic literature, which notes azelaic and mandelic peels are commonly used across age groups [1]. Wikipedia's chemical peel article does not discuss mandelic acid specifically [2].
Published evidence is limited to a 2013 sebum study in mature women and a 2022 acne trial using a combined salicylic and mandelic peel [1][3].
infobox: Sebum secretion in mature skin, acne tarda [1][3]

paras: A 2013 Polish study measured facial sebum secretion in 28 women aged 49 to 71, of whom 11 received azelaic acid peels and 17 mandelic acid peels [1]. A 2022 randomized study of adult acne (acne tarda) compared low-dose oral isotretinoin alone with isotretinoin combined with a 20% salicylic and 10% mandelic acid peel [3]. A registered trial of mandelic acid peel versus intralesional tranexamic acid for melasma has not yet begun recruiting [4].
The 2013 study's authors describe azelaic and mandelic peels as mild peels not causing side effects [1]. Wikipedia notes that light peels in general commonly cause stinging, redness and dryness [2].
